facts.statement: With the club's charter being lost, the exact date remains open to debate.
In honour of its English origins, the club has retained the English spelling of the city's name.
The Italian spelling of the city's name is Milano.
Under the fascist regime, the club was forced to bear the Italian spelling Milano.
Milan won its first Italian championship in 1901.
Milan's 1901 Italian championship interrupted a three-year hegemony of Genoa.
Milan won a further two in succession in 1906 and 1907.
The club proved successful in the first decade of its existence.
The club won several important trophies in the first decade of its existence, including the Medaglia del Re three times, the Palla Dapples 23 times and the FGNI tournament five times.
The FGNI tournament was organized by the Italian Gymnastics Federation.
The FGNI tournament was not officially recognized by the Italian Football Federation.
In 1908, Milan experienced a split.
The 1908 split was caused by internal disagreements over the signing of foreign players.
The 1908 split led to the forming of another Milan-based team, F.C. Internazionale.
Following these events, Milan did not manage to win a single domestic title until 1950–51.
Some exceptions to Milan's lack of domestic titles until 1950–51 were represented by the 1915–16 Coppa Federale and the 1917–18 Coppa Mauro.
The 1915–16 Coppa Federale and the 1917–18 Coppa Mauro were two tournaments played during the First World War.
Especially the former, the 1915–16 Coppa Federale, received a lot of attention.
The 1915–16 Coppa Federale and the 1917–18 Coppa Mauro proved to be highly competitive.
The 1915–16 Coppa Federale and the 1917–18 Coppa Mauro were not officially recognized by the Italian federation.
The 1950s saw the club return to the top of Italian football.
The club's return to the top of Italian football in the 1950s was headed by the famous Gre-No-Li Swedish trio Gunnar Gren, Gunnar Nordahl and Nils Liedholm.
